--remove-source-files should remove the source files as they are transferred and without any delays.
Canceling the operation should not result in duplicates remaining

parts.operation: --remove-source-files should remove the source files as they are transferred and without any delays.

author_semantics.intended_meaning: Remove each transferred source file as soon as its transfer completes. Canceling must leave no duplicate of a completed transfer.

text:

parts.operation: --remove-source-files should remove the source files as they are transferred and without any delays.
parts.preserve: Canceling the operation may result in duplicates remaining.

author_semantics.intended_meaning: Keep the request for immediate removal after each completed transfer and permit duplicates to remain if the operation is canceled.
author_semantics.unresolved: The request permits residual duplicates on cancellation without saying when cancellation may interrupt cleanup.

text:
With --remove-source-files, remove only the first source file to finish transferring, immediately after it transfers.
Canceling the operation should leave no duplicate of that first file.

parts.operation: With --remove-source-files, remove only the first source file to finish transferring, immediately after it transfers.

author_semantics.intended_meaning: Apply immediate source removal and cancellation without duplicates only to the first completed transfer.
author_semantics.changed_target: All transferred source files become one source file selected by transfer completion order.

text:
With `--remove-source-files`, skip removal only for the first source in the transfer list whose path is also its target path.
Removing that source would also remove its target.

parts.operation: With `--remove-source-files`, skip removal only for the first source in the transfer list whose path is also its target path.

author_semantics.intended_meaning: Protect only the first same-path source and destination pair in the transfer list from source removal.
author_semantics.changed_target: Every same-path pair becomes the first such pair in the transfer list.
author_semantics.unresolved: The request leaves open whether the list actually contains more than one same-path pair.

Duplicate path should copy shape of original path.
In 0.92 it only copied shape;

parts.preserve: In 0.92 it only copied shape;

author_semantics.unresolved: The isolated 0.92 sentence reports historical behavior. The reading of that behavior as a preference comes from the surrounding request.
